def: A French procedure by which an employer and an employee on a permanent contract agree to end the contract, subject to approval by the labour authority.

formal.ex: The parties have decided to end the employment contract by way of a [[mutual termination agreement]], in accordance with the French Labour Code.

everyday.ex: She isn't being dismissed and she isn't resigning: they've gone for a [[mutual termination]].

collocations: to enter into a mutual termination agreement
to sign a mutual termination agreement
to leave under a mutual termination agreement
note_fr: Ne traduisez pas par « conventional breach » ni « conventional rupture » : incompréhensible. Ni le droit britannique ni le droit américain ne connaissent de procédure homologuée équivalente ; on y parle de « settlement agreement » (UK) ou de « separation agreement » (US), qui sont de simples contrats.

explain.written: The rupture conventionnelle is a statutory procedure under which the employer and an employee on a permanent contract jointly agree to terminate the contract, subject to a cooling-off period and to approval by the labour authority.
explain.spoken: It's a termination by mutual agreement, with a set procedure: you meet, you sign, each side gets a cooling-off period, and then the labour authority has to approve it.

def: With both parties freely agreeing, rather than one of them deciding alone.

formal.ex: The contract may be terminated at any time [[by mutual consent]] of the parties.

everyday.ex: In the end they parted ways [[by mutual agreement]], which suited everyone.

collocations: to part company by mutual agreement
note_fr: « By common agreement » se comprend mais sonne traduit ; préférez « by mutual agreement / consent ». Attention : « mutual » s'écrit sans « e » final et l'adverbe est « mutually » (« mutually agreed »).

def: An arrangement under which an employee leaves on terms agreed with the employer rather than being dismissed or simply resigning.

formal.ex: The Company is prepared to explore a [[negotiated termination]] of the Employee's employment.
formal.ex_us: The Company is prepared to explore a [[negotiated separation]] from employment.

everyday.ex: Rather than go down the disciplinary route, they offered him an [[agreed exit]].
everyday.ex_us: Rather than go the disciplinary route, they offered him a [[negotiated exit]].

informal.ex: Rumour has it she walked away with a very decent [[exit deal]].
informal.ex_us: Word is she walked away with a very decent [[exit package]].

note_fr: « Exit » est le mot courant en anglais RH pour tout départ (« exit interview », « exit terms »). « Negotiated departure » est correct mais plus rare. Évitez « negotiated leaving ».

term.uk: to raise the possibility of an agreed exit
term.us: to raise the possibility of a negotiated exit

ipa.uk: /tə reɪz ðə ˌpɒsəˈbɪləti əv ən əˈɡriːd ˈeksɪt/
ipa.us: /tə reɪz ðə ˌpɑːsəˈbɪləti əv ə nɪˈɡoʊʃieɪtɪd ˈeɡzɪt/

def: To mention to the other party, usually for the first time, that ending the contract by agreement might be an option.

formal.ex: Either party may [[propose a mutual termination]]; neither may impose it on the other.

everyday.uk: to raise the possibility of an agreed exit
everyday.us: to raise the possibility of a negotiated exit
everyday.ex: I'd [[raise the possibility of an agreed exit]] with him informally before putting anything in writing.
everyday.ex_us: I'd [[raise the possibility of a negotiated exit]] with him informally before putting anything in writing.

informal.ex: Could you [[sound her out]] about leaving on agreed terms?

collocations: to broach the subject of an exit
to float the idea of a settlement
note_fr: « To propose » n'est pas « to offer » : on « proposes » une idée, on « offers » une somme. « To broach the subject » (aborder un sujet délicat) et « to sound someone out » (sonder quelqu'un) sont très utiles dans ce contexte.

fr: entretien (de négociation de la rupture conventionnelle)
def: A meeting at which the employer and the employee discuss whether to end the contract by agreement and on what terms.

formal.uk: meeting to discuss the terms of the termination
formal.us: meeting to discuss the terms of the termination
formal.ex: The parties shall hold at least one [[meeting to discuss the terms of the termination]] before signing the agreement.

everyday.ex: We've had two [[negotiation meetings]] so far and we're close on the figure.

informal.ex: Let's have a proper [[sit-down]] with him next week and see where he stands.

collocations: to invite someone to a meeting
note_fr: N'utilisez pas « interview » : en anglais, c'est un entretien d'embauche ou journalistique (exception : « exit interview »). Pour la rupture conventionnelle, le droit français exige au moins un entretien ; rien d'équivalent n'est imposé au Royaume-Uni ou aux États-Unis.

def: To attend a formal meeting together with a person who supports or advises you.

formal.ex: The Employee may [[be assisted by]] a fellow employee or, where the company has no staff representatives, by an external adviser from the official list.

everyday.ex: You're welcome to [[bring someone along]] to the meeting if you'd feel more comfortable.

note_fr: « Assisted » est correct dans un texte formel, mais « to assist to a meeting » est un faux ami (« assister à » = « to attend »). Au Royaume-Uni, le « right to be accompanied » légal ne vise que les entretiens disciplinaires et de réclamation ; aux États-Unis, il n'existe en principe qu'en milieu syndiqué.

def: A fixed period after signing during which either party may change its mind and cancel the agreement without giving a reason.

formal.ex: Each party has a [[withdrawal period]] of fifteen calendar days from the day after signature.

everyday.ex: Nothing goes to the labour authority until the [[cooling-off period]] is over.
everyday.ex_us: Nothing goes to the labor authority until the [[cooling-off period]] is over.

collocations: once the cooling-off period has elapsed
note_fr: « Retractation period » n'existe pas. En droit français, le délai est de quinze jours calendaires pour chacune des parties. Aux États-Unis, on parle de « revocation period » pour le délai dont dispose le salarié de 40 ans et plus après signature d'une renonciation à recours.

def: To cancel one's acceptance of an agreement within the period allowed for doing so.

formal.uk: to exercise one's right of withdrawal
formal.us: to exercise one's right of withdrawal
formal.ex: Either party may [[exercise its right of withdrawal]] by letter delivered to the other party within the period.

everyday.ex: He's got until the 20th to [[change his mind]], so let's not announce anything yet.
everyday.ex_us: He has until the 20th to [[change his mind]], so let's not announce anything yet.

informal.ex: If she [[pulls out]] now, we're back to square one.
informal.ex_us: If she [[backs out]] now, we're back to square one.

collocations: to exercise the right of withdrawal
to go back on an agreement
note_fr: « To retract » s'emploie pour une déclaration ou une démission (« to retract a statement »), pas pour un accord. Notez la construction : « to withdraw FROM an agreement » mais « to withdraw an offer ».

def: Formal approval by the French labour authority, without which a mutual termination agreement has no effect.

formal.ex: The validity of the agreement is conditional upon its [[approval by the labour authority]].
formal.ex_us: The validity of the agreement is conditional upon its [[approval by the labor authority]].

everyday.ex: We can't confirm his leaving date until we have [[sign-off from the labour authority]].
everyday.ex_us: We can't confirm his last day until we have [[sign-off from the labor authority]].

note_fr: « Homologation » existe en anglais mais relève du vocabulaire technique (automobile, sport) : personne ne le comprendra en RH. Rien d'équivalent au Royaume-Uni ni aux États-Unis, où un accord de départ ne passe devant aucune administration.

explain.written: Homologation is the formal approval of a mutual termination agreement by the regional labour authority, which checks that the procedure was followed and that both parties consented freely.
explain.spoken: Once it's signed, the agreement has to be approved by the labour authority. Until that's done, the contract simply carries on.

def: The formal request sent to the labour authority, after the cooling-off period, asking it to approve the agreement.

formal.ex: Upon expiry of the withdrawal period, the [[application for approval]] shall be submitted by whichever party acts first.

everyday.uk: to send it off for approval
everyday.us: to send it off for approval
everyday.ex: The cooling-off period ends on Friday, so we'll [[send it off for approval]] on Monday.

note_fr: « Demand » est un faux ami : « a demand » est une exigence. Une demande administrative est « an application » ou « a request ». « To file » est plus américain, « to lodge » plus britannique ; « to submit » passe partout.

def: Approval that is treated as given because the authority has not replied within the time allowed.

formal.uk: to be deemed to have been approved
formal.us: to be deemed to have been approved
formal.ex: If the authority has not responded within the review period, the agreement shall [[be deemed to have been approved]].

everyday.ex: With the labour authority, [[no news is good news]]: if they stay silent, it's approved.
everyday.ex_us: With the labor authority, [[no news is good news]]: if they stay silent, it's approved.

collocations: in the absence of a reply
note_fr: « Deemed » (réputé) est le mot juridique clé : « deemed approval », « deemed to have resigned ». Pour un interlocuteur anglo-saxon, précisez toujours que le silence de l'administration vaut ici acceptation : l'idée lui est peu familière.

def: A decision by the labour authority not to approve the agreement, so that the employment contract continues.

formal.ex: Should the authority [[refuse approval]], the employment contract shall continue on its existing terms.

everyday.ex: The agreement was [[turned down]] because the payment was below the legal minimum.

informal.ex: The first application got [[knocked back]] over a wrong date.
informal.ex_us: The first application got [[kicked back]] over a wrong date.

note_fr: « To refuse » se construit avec un nom ou « to + verbe » : « the authority refused to approve it », jamais « refused that ». « To knock back » est britannique et familier ; l'américain dirait « to kick back » ou « to bounce ».

def: The sum the employer must pay an employee who leaves under a French mutual termination agreement, which cannot be lower than the statutory dismissal payment.

formal.ex: The Employee shall receive a [[specific termination payment]] in a gross amount of not less than the statutory severance entitlement.

everyday.ex: The [[termination payment]] is the legal minimum plus four months' salary on top.
everyday.ex_us: The [[severance payment]] is the legal minimum plus four months' salary on top.

collocations: not less than the statutory minimum
note_fr: « Indemnity » est un faux ami : en anglais juridique, c'est une garantie contre un préjudice subi par autrui. Pour une somme versée au départ, dites « payment », « compensation » ou « severance ».

explain.written: The indemnité spécifique de rupture conventionnelle is the payment due to an employee who leaves under a mutual termination agreement; its amount is negotiated but may not be less than the statutory dismissal payment.
explain.spoken: It's the payment the employee gets on the way out. You can negotiate the amount, but there's a legal floor you can't go below.

def: Money paid by an employer to an employee because the employment is ending.

formal.ex: The [[termination payment]] shall be made within twenty-eight days of the Termination Date.
formal.ex_us: [[Severance pay]] shall be paid in a lump sum within thirty days of the Separation Date.

everyday.ex: They've put together a [[severance package]] worth about nine months' salary.

informal.ex: He left with a six-figure [[pay-off]].

note_fr: « Severance » s'emploie surtout aux États-Unis, où il n'est dû que si un contrat ou une politique interne le prévoit. Au Royaume-Uni, on distingue « redundancy pay » (licenciement économique) et « termination payment » (terme général). « Golden handshake » désigne familièrement un départ très bien indemnisé.

def: The day on which the employment contract legally comes to an end.

formal.ex: The Employee's employment shall end on 30 June (the '[[Termination Date]]').
formal.ex_us: The Employee's employment shall end on June 30 (the '[[Separation Date]]').

everyday.ex: Have we agreed a [[leaving date]] with her yet?
everyday.ex_us: Have we agreed on a [[last day]] with her yet?

note_fr: Pour une rupture conventionnelle, la date ne peut pas être antérieure au lendemain de l'homologation. Notez « to bring forward » (avancer) et « to push back » (reculer) ; « to agree a date » est britannique, l'américain dit « to agree on a date ».

def: Agreement given voluntarily by a person who understands what he or she is agreeing to.

formal.ex: Each party confirms that it has given its [[free and informed consent]] to this agreement.
formal.ex_us: Employee acknowledges that he has given his [[knowing and voluntary consent]] to this Agreement.

everyday.uk: to agree of one's own free will
everyday.us: to agree of one's own free will
everyday.ex: We need to be sure she's [[agreeing of her own free will]] and knows what she's signing.

collocations: to enter into an agreement knowingly and voluntarily
note_fr: Aux États-Unis, la formule consacrée pour la validité d'une renonciation à recours est « knowing and voluntary ». « Enlightened consent » est un calque à éviter.

def: Consent that is legally defective because it was obtained by mistake, deception or pressure.

formal.ex: Evidence of harassment at the time of signature may [[vitiate consent]] and render the agreement void.

everyday.ex: If he can show he [[signed under pressure]], a court could set the whole agreement aside.

informal.ex: She says she was [[strong-armed into signing]] on the spot.

note_fr: « Vice of consent » fait sourire (« vice » = le vice moral). Les notions de common law sont « duress » (contrainte), « undue influence » (abus d'influence), « misrepresentation » (dol) et « mistake » (erreur). « To set aside » = annuler (par un juge).

def: A French scheme, set up by a collective agreement approved by the labour authority, under which employees may volunteer to leave on agreed terms without any redundancy procedure.

formal.ex: The [[collective mutual termination scheme]] sets a maximum number of departures and rules out any compulsory dismissal.
formal.ex_us: The [[collective mutual termination program]] sets a maximum number of departures and rules out any involuntary termination.

everyday.ex: Applications for the [[voluntary exit scheme]] close at the end of March.
everyday.ex_us: Applications for the [[voluntary exit program]] close at the end of March.

collocations: to open the scheme to volunteers
note_fr: « Scheme » est neutre en anglais britannique (dispositif) mais péjoratif en américain (combine) : dites « program » ou « plan » aux États-Unis. Les équivalents fonctionnels sont le « voluntary exit scheme » britannique et le « voluntary separation program » américain, sans le cadre légal français.

explain.written: The rupture conventionnelle collective is a framework, negotiated with the trade unions and approved by the labour authority, allowing a set number of employees to leave voluntarily on agreed terms outside any redundancy procedure.
explain.spoken: It's a voluntary exit scheme agreed with the unions: people can put themselves forward to leave with a package, and nobody can be forced out.

def: To deal with the last small matters that remain before something is finished.

formal.ex: The parties shall cooperate in good faith to [[finalise outstanding matters]] before the Termination Date.
formal.ex_us: The parties shall cooperate in good faith to [[finalize outstanding matters]] before the Separation Date.

everyday.ex: I've got two weeks left, which should be enough to [[tie up loose ends]].
everyday.ex_us: I have two weeks left, which should be enough to [[tie up loose ends]].

collocations: to leave things in good order
note_fr: « Outstanding » signifie ici « en suspens, restant à régler » (« outstanding holiday », « outstanding expenses ») et non « remarquable ». « To wrap up » = boucler, conclure.

def: To end a working relationship without conflict or bad feeling.

formal.ex: The parties wish to [[part amicably]] and to settle all matters between them.

everyday.ex: It's a small sector, so it's in everyone's interest to [[part on good terms]].

informal.ex: It didn't work out, but there are [[no hard feelings]] on either side.

note_fr: « Amicably » (à l'amiable) et non « amiably » (aimablement) : deux mots distincts. « To part company with someone » est aussi l'euphémisme journalistique pour un départ. « Don't burn your bridges » : ne coupez pas les ponts.

def: A written agreement that ends or prevents a dispute, usually by one party paying a sum and the other giving up its claims.

formal.ex: This [[settlement agreement]] is intended to bring to an end any dispute arising from the termination of the Employee's employment.

everyday.ex: Their lawyer has hinted they'd be open to a [[settlement]].

informal.ex: I think there's a [[deal]] to be done here.

collocations: to enter into a settlement agreement
note_fr: Faux ami majeur : « a transaction » est une opération commerciale ou bancaire, jamais un accord mettant fin à un litige. En droit français, la transaction suppose des concessions réciproques et, après un licenciement, se signe une fois la rupture notifiée. Au Royaume-Uni, le « settlement agreement » (ex-« compromise agreement ») n'est valable que si le salarié a été conseillé par un conseiller indépendant.

def: To end a dispute by agreement instead of letting a court decide it.

formal.ex: The parties have [[reached a settlement]] on the terms set out below.

everyday.ex: My advice would be to [[settle]] now rather than spend two years in court.

informal.ex: They'd rather [[do a deal]] than see this in the papers.
informal.ex_us: They'd rather [[cut a deal]] than see this in the papers.

collocations: to settle for a lower amount
note_fr: « To transact » ne convient pas. Distinguez « to settle a claim » (régler un litige), « to settle for » (se contenter de) et « to settle in » (s'installer). « To compromise a claim » existe en anglais juridique britannique, mais « to compromise » signifie le plus souvent « compromettre ».

def: Something given up by each party in order to reach an agreement.

formal.ex: Under French law, a settlement is valid only if it records [[mutual concessions]] by the parties.

everyday.ex: There has to be some [[give and take]]: he drops the claim, we improve the payment.

note_fr: En common law, la notion voisine est la « consideration » (contrepartie), condition de validité de tout contrat : d'où la formule « in consideration of the payment... ». Ce n'est pas « la considération ». « Give and take » est invariable et très courant à l'oral.

def: The sum paid under a settlement agreement in exchange for the other party giving up its claims.

formal.ex: The Company shall pay the Employee a [[settlement payment]] of EUR 25,000 gross, in addition to his contractual entitlements.
formal.ex_us: The Company shall pay Employee a [[settlement payment]] of EUR 25,000 gross, in addition to his contractual entitlements.

everyday.ex: We're still some way apart on the [[settlement figure]].

note_fr: Précisez toujours « gross » ou « net » et ce qui s'ajoute (« in addition to », « over and above ») ou est inclus (« inclusive of »). Rappel : pas d'« indemnity » ici. « Figure » = chiffre, montant ; « to agree a figure » (UK) / « to agree on a number » (US).

def: An undertaking by which a person gives up the right to bring legal proceedings about a particular matter.

formal.ex: The [[waiver of claims]] in clause 5 covers all claims relating to the performance or termination of the contract.

everyday.uk: to agree not to bring a claim
everyday.ex: In return for the payment, she [[agrees not to bring a claim]] against the company.
everyday.ex_us: In return for the payment, she [[agrees not to sue]] the company.

informal.ex: Get advice first, because you're effectively [[signing away your rights]].

note_fr: « Renunciation » est rare et littéraire ; le terme juridique est « waiver ». Certains droits ne peuvent pas faire l'objet d'une renonciation : au Royaume-Uni, la renonciation à des droits légaux n'est valable que dans un « settlement agreement » conforme ou un accord conclu via l'Acas ; aux États-Unis, on ne peut pas renoncer au droit de saisir l'agence fédérale chargée de l'égalité (EEOC).

fr: à titre de règlement global et définitif
def: As a payment or agreement that completely and permanently ends all the claims concerned.

formal.uk: in full and final settlement of
formal.us: in full and final settlement of
formal.ex: The Employee accepts the payment [[in full and final settlement of]] all claims he has or may have against the Company.
formal.ex_us: Employee accepts the payment [[in full and final settlement of]] all claims he has or may have against the Company.

everyday.us: to put the matter to rest
everyday.ex: The idea is to [[draw a line under]] the whole thing so that both sides can move on.
everyday.ex_us: The idea is to [[put the matter to rest]] so that both sides can move on.

collocations: to close the matter once and for all
note_fr: Le doublet « full and final » est figé : ne dites pas « total and definitive ». Attention, « definitive » signifie « qui fait autorité » (« the definitive guide »), pas « définitif » au sens de « final ».

def: A contractual statement by which one party frees the other from liability for the claims described.

formal.ex: The Employee hereby [[releases and discharges]] the Company and its affiliates from all claims arising out of his employment.
formal.ex_us: Employee hereby [[releases and discharges]] the Company and its affiliates from any and all claims arising out of his employment.

everyday.ex: No [[release]], no payment: that's the standard position in the States.

note_fr: « Release » (libération, décharge) est le terme américain habituel là où le Britannique dit « waiver » ou « settlement ». Un « mutual release » lie les deux parties. Ne confondez pas avec « press release » (communiqué).

fr: accord de départ avec renonciation à recours (pratique américaine)
def: In the US, a contract under which a departing employee receives severance pay in exchange for giving up the right to sue the employer.

formal.ex: The payment is conditional upon the Employee signing a [[settlement agreement]] in the form attached.
formal.ex_us: Payment is conditioned upon Employee's execution of a [[severance agreement and general release]] in the form attached.

everyday.ex: We'll send her the [[settlement agreement]] once her solicitor's details are confirmed.
everyday.ex_us: We'll send her the [[separation agreement]] once legal has signed off on it.

collocations: to review the agreement with an attorney
note_fr: Aux États-Unis, l'indemnité n'est en général pas due par la loi : elle est offerte en échange de la signature d'un « release ». « To execute an agreement » signifie le signer en bonne et due forme, pas l'exécuter. « Conditioned upon » est américain ; « conditional upon » britannique.

fr: sous toutes réserves (discussions de règlement confidentielles)
def: Describes settlement discussions or letters which cannot later be used as evidence against the party who made them.

formal.ex: This offer is made [[on a without prejudice basis]] and may not be referred to in any proceedings.
formal.ex_us: This offer is made [[for settlement purposes only]] and may not be used as evidence in any proceeding.

everyday.ex: Can we have a [[without prejudice]] conversation about how we might resolve this?
everyday.ex_us: Can we have a [[confidential settlement discussion]] about how we might resolve this?

collocations: without prejudice save as to costs
note_fr: « Without prejudice » ne veut pas dire « sans préjugé ». Au Royaume-Uni, la protection suppose qu'un litige existe déjà et qu'il s'agisse d'une tentative sincère de règlement : écrire la mention en tête de lettre ne suffit pas. Aux États-Unis, l'expression est peu employée dans ce sens ; les règles de preuve y protègent les offres de règlement.

fr: « protected conversation » (négociation préalable à la rupture, droit britannique)
def: In Great Britain, a confidential discussion about ending someone's employment on agreed terms, which generally cannot be used as evidence in an ordinary unfair dismissal claim.

formal.ex: Evidence of [[pre-termination negotiations]] is inadmissible in ordinary unfair dismissal proceedings, save where there has been improper behaviour.
formal.ex_us: Under British law, evidence of [[pre-termination negotiations]] is inadmissible in ordinary unfair dismissal proceedings, save where there has been improper behavior.

everyday.ex: HR asked him in for a [[protected conversation]] and offered him three months' pay to go.

note_fr: Notion propre au droit britannique, sans équivalent américain ni français. À la différence du « without prejudice », elle ne suppose aucun litige préexistant, mais elle ne joue ni pour les demandes fondées sur une discrimination ni en cas de comportement abusif de l'employeur (pression excessive, par exemple).

def: Said privately and unofficially, on the understanding that it will not be quoted or noted.

formal.ex: The information was disclosed [[in confidence]] and must not be passed on.

everyday.ex: [[Off the record]], would he consider leaving if the terms were right?

informal.ex: [[Between you and me]], I don't think she wants to stay anyway.

note_fr: « Off the record » n'offre aucune protection juridique : c'est une convention de politesse. Au Royaume-Uni, seuls le « without prejudice » et la « protected conversation » empêchent réellement qu'un échange soit produit en justice. Avec trait d'union devant un nom : « an off-the-record chat ».

def: Advice given to the employee by a lawyer or other qualified adviser who does not act for the employer.

formal.ex: The Employee confirms that he has [[received independent legal advice]] from a relevant independent adviser on the terms and effect of this agreement.
formal.ex_us: Employee is hereby advised in writing to [[consult with an attorney]] before signing this Agreement.

everyday.ex: You'll need to [[take legal advice]] before you sign; the agreement isn't binding otherwise.
everyday.ex_us: You should [[talk to a lawyer]] before you sign; we're required to tell you that.

note_fr: « Advice » est indénombrable : « some advice », « a piece of advice », jamais « an advice » ni « advices ». Au Royaume-Uni, ce conseil indépendant est une condition de validité du « settlement agreement » ; aux États-Unis, l'employeur doit seulement inviter par écrit le salarié de 40 ans et plus à consulter un avocat.

def: A sum paid by the employer to cover part or all of what the employee's lawyer charges for advising on the agreement.

formal.ex: The Company shall make a [[contribution towards legal fees]] of up to GBP 500 plus VAT, payable direct to the Employee's solicitors.
formal.ex_us: The Company shall make a [[contribution toward attorney's fees]] of up to USD 1,000, payable directly to Employee's counsel.

everyday.ex: We normally [[cover the employee's legal costs]] up to a fixed amount.

collocations: each party bears its own costs
note_fr: « Fees » = honoraires ; « costs » = frais de justice au sens large. « Towards » (UK) / « toward » (US). Cette participation est une pratique britannique quasi systématique, non une obligation légale ; elle est rare aux États-Unis. « Honoraries » n'existe pas dans ce sens.

def: The time an employee is given to think about a proposed agreement and take advice before deciding whether to sign it.

formal.ex: The Employee shall have a reasonable [[period in which to consider]] the offer and to take advice.
formal.ex_us: Employee acknowledges that he has been given a [[period in which to consider]] this Agreement of at least twenty-one days.

everyday.ex: Take the draft home; you've got plenty of [[time to think it over]].
everyday.ex_us: Take the draft home; you have plenty of [[time to think it over]].

informal.ex: Don't sign today. [[Sleep on it]] and call me tomorrow.

note_fr: Aux États-Unis, la loi fédérale impose, pour qu'un salarié de 40 ans et plus renonce valablement à agir pour discrimination liée à l'âge, un délai de réflexion d'au moins 21 jours, puis 7 jours pour révoquer sa signature. Au Royaume-Uni, le code de l'Acas recommande d'ordinaire au moins dix jours calendaires. Ne confondez pas ce délai, antérieur à la signature, avec le « cooling-off period », postérieur.

def: A clause in which a party promises not to make damaging statements about the other.

formal.ex: The [[non-disparagement clause]] binds both the Employee and the Company's senior officers.

everyday.uk: to agree not to criticise each other
everyday.us: to agree not to criticize each other
everyday.ex: Both sides [[agree not to criticise each other]] in public, and that includes social media.
everyday.ex_us: Both sides [[agree not to criticize each other]] in public, and that includes social media.

collocations: to be in breach of the clause
whether orally, in writing or online
note_fr: Aucune de ces clauses ne peut empêcher un signalement protégé (« whistleblowing ») ni un témoignage devant une autorité, des deux côtés de l'Atlantique. Demandez toujours une clause « mutual » : par défaut, elle ne lie souvent que le salarié.

def: To say things that damage the reputation of a person or an organisation.

formal.ex: The Employee shall not [[make disparaging statements about]] the Company, its officers or its employees.

everyday.ex: He's been [[running the company down]] to clients ever since he left.

informal.ex: The last thing we want is her [[bad-mouthing]] us all over LinkedIn.

note_fr: « To denigrate » existe mais reste livresque ; « to disparage » est le terme des contrats, « to run down » et « to bad-mouth » ceux de l'oral. « To criticise » est plus faible : une critique peut être fondée.

fr: garder les termes de l'accord confidentiels
def: Not to tell anyone what an agreement says, apart from the people the agreement allows you to tell.

formal.uk: to keep the terms of this agreement confidential
formal.us: to keep the terms of this Agreement confidential
formal.ex: The parties shall [[keep the terms of this agreement confidential]], save as required by law or for the purpose of taking professional advice.
formal.ex_us: The parties shall [[keep the terms of this Agreement confidential]], except as required by law or for the purpose of obtaining professional advice.

everyday.ex: You can tell your partner and your accountant; otherwise please [[keep it to yourself]].

informal.ex: Let's [[keep it under wraps]] until the paperwork's signed.

collocations: the existence and terms of the agreement
to disclose to one's spouse or professional advisers
note_fr: Ne confondez pas « confidential » (confidentiel) et « confident » (sûr de soi). « Save as » (UK, soutenu) = « except as » (US). Prévoyez toujours les exceptions usuelles : conjoint, conseils, administration fiscale, organisme d'assurance chômage.

def: A contract or clause under which a person undertakes not to reveal certain information, for example the circumstances of a departure.

formal.ex: Nothing in this [[non-disclosure agreement]] prevents the Employee from making a protected disclosure or reporting a criminal offence.
formal.ex_us: Nothing in this [[nondisclosure agreement]] prevents Employee from filing a charge with, or communicating with, any government agency.

everyday.ex: She signed an [[NDA]] as part of the settlement, so she can't discuss the details.

informal.ex: The press called it a [[gagging clause]], which didn't help the company's image.
informal.ex_us: The press called it a [[gag clause]], which didn't help the company's image.

collocations: to be bound by an NDA
note_fr: Sujet sensible : au Royaume-Uni comme dans plusieurs États américains, la loi limite l'usage des NDA pour étouffer des faits de harcèlement ou de discrimination, et aucun NDA ne peut interdire un signalement aux autorités. « Carve-out » = exception expressément prévue. « Gagging clause » est péjoratif.

fr: références convenues (texte de recommandation annexé à l'accord)
def: A reference whose wording is negotiated in advance and attached to the settlement agreement, which the employer undertakes to give to any future employer who asks.

formal.ex: On request from a prospective employer, the Company shall provide a [[reference in the agreed form]] set out in Schedule 2.
formal.ex_us: In response to any inquiry from a prospective employer, the Company shall provide a [[neutral reference]] limited to dates of employment and last position held.

everyday.ex: The money matters less to him than getting a decent [[agreed reference]].

collocations: to agree the wording of a reference
note_fr: Pratique typiquement britannique, où l'employeur n'a en principe aucune obligation de fournir une référence. Aux États-Unis, par crainte des procès, beaucoup d'entreprises ne confirment que les dates et le poste (« neutral reference »). Le certificat de travail français n'est pas une « reference » : il ne porte aucune appréciation.

def: A statement by a former employer about a person's work and character, given to someone who may employ that person.

formal.ex: The Company will provide a written [[reference]] upon request.
formal.ex_us: The Company will provide a [[letter of recommendation]] upon request.

everyday.ex: Of course I'll [[give you a reference]]; just put my name down.
everyday.ex_us: Of course I'll [[give you a reference]]; just list my name.

note_fr: « A reference » désigne le document ou la personne aux États-Unis ; au Royaume-Uni, la personne est « a referee » (qui n'est pas ici un arbitre). « To take up references » (UK) = contacter les anciens employeurs. « Recommendation letter » se dit, mais « letter of recommendation » est plus naturel.

def: A statement about someone's departure whose wording both sides have approved before it is sent to staff or clients.

formal.ex: The Employee's departure shall be communicated internally by means of an [[announcement in the agreed form]].
formal.ex_us: Employee's departure shall be communicated internally by means of a [[mutually agreed announcement]].

everyday.uk: to agree what to tell people
everyday.us: to agree on what to tell people
everyday.ex: Before anything goes out, we need to [[agree what to tell people]].
everyday.ex_us: Before anything goes out, we need to [[agree on what to tell people]].

informal.ex: [[The party line]] is that he's leaving to pursue other opportunities.

collocations: to wish someone well for the future
note_fr: « To pursue other opportunities / interests » est la formule consacrée, que tout le monde lit comme le signe d'un départ négocié. « Communication » est rarement le bon mot pour une annonce ponctuelle : dites « announcement » ou « statement ».

def: Without accepting that one has done anything legally wrong.

formal.ex: This agreement is entered into [[without any admission of liability]] on the part of the Company.

everyday.ex: We're paying to close the matter, but we [[are not admitting any wrongdoing]].

note_fr: « Liability » = responsabilité juridique (ce dont on doit répondre) ; « responsibility » = responsabilité au sens de mission ou de devoir moral. « Without recognition of responsibility » serait un calque.

def: A payment made as a gesture of goodwill, which the payer has no legal obligation to make.

formal.ex: The Company shall pay the Employee an [[ex gratia payment]] of GBP 20,000 by way of compensation for loss of employment.
formal.ex_us: The Company shall pay Employee an [[ex gratia payment]] of USD 20,000 as additional consideration for the release below.

everyday.ex: On top of his notice pay, they've offered a [[goodwill payment]] of two months' salary.

informal.ex: They threw in an extra month as a [[sweetener]].

collocations: by way of compensation for loss of employment
note_fr: Expression latine courante en anglais juridique, surtout britannique ; prononcez « eks GRAY-sha ». Au Royaume-Uni, c'est la part « ex gratia » d'une indemnité de rupture qui bénéficie en principe de l'exonération fiscale à hauteur de 30 000 livres ; les sommes contractuelles (préavis, congés) restent imposables.

fr: régime fiscal et social de l'indemnité
def: The way a payment is taxed and whether social security contributions are due on it.

formal.uk: subject to tax and social security contributions
formal.us: subject to applicable taxes and withholdings
formal.ex: Any amount above the exempt threshold shall be [[subject to tax and social security contributions]].
formal.ex_us: All payments under this Agreement shall be [[subject to applicable taxes and withholdings]].

everyday.ex: Part of the payment should be [[tax-free]], but check the exact figure with payroll.

note_fr: « Social charges » est un calque : dites « social security contributions » (ou « National Insurance contributions » au Royaume-Uni, « payroll taxes » aux États-Unis). « Withholding » = retenue à la source. Ne donnez jamais de chiffre de mémoire : les plafonds d'exonération changent souvent.

def: To tell the other party what you are prepared to pay or accept in order to reach an agreement.

formal.ex: The Company is prepared to [[make an offer]] in order to resolve this matter without recourse to litigation.

everyday.uk: to put an offer on the table
everyday.us: to put an offer on the table
everyday.ex: We've [[put an offer on the table]]; it's up to them to come back to us.

informal.ex: I'd let them [[name a figure]] first.
informal.ex_us: I'd let them [[name a number]] first.

note_fr: On « makes » une offre, on ne la « does » pas. « The offer is on the table » = l'offre tient toujours ; « to take the offer off the table » = la retirer. « An opening offer » est la première offre, volontairement basse.

def: An offer made in reply to another offer, on different terms.

formal.ex: The Employee's adviser submitted a [[counter-proposal]] on 3 March.
formal.ex_us: Employee's counsel submitted a [[counterproposal]] on March 3.

everyday.ex: They turned down four months and [[came back with]] eight.

note_fr: Deux sens à connaître : la contre-proposition dans une négociation, et l'offre faite à un démissionnaire pour le retenir (« they made her a counter-offer to stay »). « To split the difference » = couper la poire en deux. Trait d'union en anglais britannique, mot soudé en américain.

def: The extent to which a party is able or willing to change its position during discussions.

formal.ex: There is limited [[scope for negotiation]] on the amount, which has been approved at group level.
formal.ex_us: There is limited [[room for negotiation]] on the amount, which has been approved at the corporate level.

everyday.ex: I've got a bit of [[room for manoeuvre]] on the date, less so on the money.
everyday.ex_us: I have a little [[room to maneuver]] on the date, less so on the money.

informal.ex: Is there any [[wiggle room]] on the figure?

collocations: to have a mandate to negotiate
note_fr: « Margin of negotiation » est un calque. Orthographe : « manoeuvre » (UK) / « maneuver » (US). « Leeway » = latitude. « I'd need to check my mandate » : formule utile quand on doit en référer au client.

def: To come to an agreement in which each side accepts less than it first asked for.

formal.ex: After two meetings, the parties [[reached a compromise]] on the amount of the payment.

everyday.ex: If they drop the bonus claim, I think we could [[meet them halfway]] on the payment.

informal.ex: You're at six, we're at four: shall we just [[split the difference]]?
informal.ex_us: You're at six, we're at four: why don't we just [[split the difference]]?

note_fr: Faux ami partiel : « a compromise » est un compromis, mais « compromising » signifie « compromettant » et « to compromise security » = mettre en péril. « Compromis » au sens immobilier ne se traduit pas ainsi. « Common ground » est indénombrable : pas d'article.

fr: tout litige né ou à naître de l'exécution ou de la rupture du contrat

term.uk: claims arising out of the employment or its termination
term.us: claims arising out of the employment or its termination

ipa.uk: /kleɪmz əˈraɪzɪŋ aʊt əv ði ɪmˈplɔɪmənt ɔːr ɪts ˌtɜːmɪˈneɪʃ(ə)n/
ipa.us: /kleɪmz əˈraɪzɪŋ aʊt əv ði ɪmˈplɔɪmənt ɔːr ɪts ˌtɜːrmɪˈneɪʃ(ə)n/

def: All the legal complaints an employee has, or might later have, in connection with the job or the way it ended.

formal.uk: arising out of or in connection with
formal.us: arising out of or relating to
formal.ex: The waiver extends to all claims, whether present or future, [[arising out of or in connection with]] the Employee's employment or its termination.
formal.ex_us: The release extends to any and all claims, known or unknown, [[arising out of or relating to]] Employee's employment or its termination.

everyday.ex: Once he signs, he can't sue over [[anything to do with]] his job or the way it ended.

collocations: the claims listed in the schedule
note_fr: « Né ou à naître » se rend par « present or future » ou, aux États-Unis, « known or unknown ». Au Royaume-Uni, une renonciation générale ne suffit pas pour les droits légaux : l'accord doit viser les demandes particulières concernées, d'où les longues listes de « claims » en annexe.

def: The likelihood that a matter will end up in court and what it could cost if it does.

formal.ex: In view of the [[litigation risk]], we recommend that a settlement be explored before any dismissal is notified.

everyday.ex: Worst case, our [[exposure]] is around twelve months' salary plus legal costs.

informal.uk: what we're on the hook for
informal.us: what we're on the hook for
informal.ex: I need to know [[what we're on the hook for]] if this goes wrong.

collocations: the cost of defending a claim
note_fr: « Contentious risk » ne se dit pas. « Exposure » (indénombrable) est le mot que vos clients anglophones emploieront : « What's our exposure? ». « To be on the hook for » (familier, surtout américain) = devoir assumer, être redevable de.

fr: protocole d'accord préalable (points clés de l'accord)
def: A short document listing the main points agreed in a negotiation, before the full agreement is drafted.

formal.ex: The [[heads of terms]] are not intended to be legally binding and remain subject to contract.
formal.ex_us: The [[term sheet]] is non-binding and remains subject to execution of a definitive agreement.

everyday.ex: We've got [[the outline of a deal]]; the lawyers can now turn it into a proper agreement.
everyday.ex_us: We have [[the outline of a deal]]; the lawyers can now turn it into a formal agreement.

informal.ex: Just send me [[the bare bones]] for now: amount, date, reference.

collocations: to draw up heads of terms
note_fr: « Protocol » est un faux ami : en anglais, c'est une procédure ou une étiquette, pas un accord. « Subject to contract » (UK) signale que rien n'engage les parties tant que l'accord définitif n'est pas signé ; l'équivalent américain est « non-binding ».

def: A general agreement on the main points, with the details still to be settled.

formal.ex: The parties have reached an [[agreement in principle]], subject to board approval.

everyday.ex: He's [[agreed in principle]]; he just wants to see it in writing.

informal.ex: We [[shook on it]] yesterday, but nothing's signed yet.

note_fr: Orthographe : « in principle » (en principe) et non « in principal » (« principal » = principal, ou proviseur). « In principle » laisse entendre une réserve, comme en français. « To firm up » = arrêter définitivement.

def: To tell one's manager or colleagues that one has decided to leave.

formal.uk: to notify the employer of one's decision to leave
formal.us: to notify the employer of one's decision to leave
formal.ex: The Employee [[notified the Company of her decision to leave]] by letter dated 4 May.
formal.ex_us: The Employee [[notified the Company of her decision to leave]] by letter dated May 4.

everyday.ex: Have you [[told Sarah you're leaving]], or should I keep quiet for now?

informal.ex: I'm dreading [[breaking the news]] to the team.

collocations: to hand in a resignation letter
note_fr: « To announce » se construit avec « to » devant la personne : « she announced her departure TO the team », jamais « she announced the team ». « To break the news » s'emploie pour une nouvelle délicate.

def: A letter in which an employee tells the employer that he or she is leaving the job.

formal.ex: The notice period runs from the date on which the Company receives [[written notice of resignation]].

everyday.ex: Keep your [[resignation letter]] short: the date, your last day and a word of thanks.

collocations: to put one's resignation in writing
note_fr: En droit français, la démission n'est soumise à aucune forme légale, mais l'écrit sert de preuve et fait courir le préavis. Prononciation : le « g » de « resign » est muet, celui de « resignation » se prononce. Faux ami : « resignation » signifie aussi « résignation ».

fr: prendre acte de la démission / l'accepter
def: To confirm formally to an employee that the employer has received the resignation and will act on it.

formal.uk: to acknowledge receipt of a resignation
formal.us: to acknowledge receipt of a resignation
formal.ex: We [[acknowledge receipt of your resignation]] dated 2 June and confirm that your last day of employment will be 1 September.
formal.ex_us: We [[acknowledge receipt of your resignation]] dated June 2 and confirm that your last day of employment will be September 1.

everyday.ex: I've [[accepted her resignation]], though I did try to talk her out of it.
everyday.ex_us: I [[accepted her resignation]], though I did try to talk her out of it.

collocations: to talk someone out of resigning
note_fr: Juridiquement, une démission n'a pas besoin d'être « acceptée » : c'est un acte unilatéral, en France comme au Royaume-Uni. On « accepte » par courtoisie et pour fixer la date. « To acknowledge » = accuser réception, prendre acte. « To talk someone out of » = dissuader.

def: Expressed so plainly that there can be no doubt about what the person means.

formal.ex: A resignation is valid only where the employee has expressed a [[clear and unequivocal]] intention to leave.

everyday.uk: to leave no room for doubt
everyday.us: to leave no room for doubt
everyday.ex: His email [[leaves no room for doubt]]: he's going, and he says when.

note_fr: Critère commun aux droits français et britannique : une démission ambiguë ou donnée sous la contrainte peut être remise en cause. « Non-equivocal » n'existe pas : c'est « unequivocal » (adverbe : « unequivocally »), ou « unambiguous ».

def: To tell the employer that one no longer wishes to resign, after having done so.

formal.ex: Once notice has been given, the Employee may [[withdraw his resignation]] only with the Company's consent.
formal.ex_us: Once notice has been given, the Employee may [[rescind his resignation]] only with the Company's consent.

everyday.ex: She rang the next morning asking to [[take back her resignation]].
everyday.ex_us: She called the next morning asking to [[take back her resignation]].

informal.ex: Apparently he's [[having second thoughts]] about leaving.

note_fr: En principe, une démission valablement donnée ne peut être retirée qu'avec l'accord de l'employeur, en France comme au Royaume-Uni. « To come back on » est un calque ; « to go back on » existe mais se dit d'une promesse ou d'une parole donnée.

fr: démission donnée sous le coup de la colère
def: A resignation announced in anger or distress, which the employee may not really have meant.

formal.uk: resignation given in the heat of the moment
formal.us: resignation given in the heat of the moment
formal.ex: An employer should be cautious about relying on a [[resignation given in the heat of the moment]].

everyday.uk: to resign in the heat of the moment
everyday.us: to resign in the heat of the moment
everyday.ex: He [[resigned in the heat of the moment]] after a row with his manager; give him a day to calm down.
everyday.ex_us: He [[resigned in the heat of the moment]] after an argument with his manager; give him a day to calm down.

informal.ex: She said 'I quit' and [[stormed out]]. Does that count as resigning?

collocations: to give someone time to cool off
to check whether they meant it
note_fr: En France comme au Royaume-Uni, les juges hésitent à tenir pour acquise une démission lancée sous le coup de l'émotion : mieux vaut laisser passer un court délai et demander confirmation par écrit. « A row » (UK, rime avec « now ») = une dispute.

def: Starting from now, with no notice period.

formal.ex: I hereby resign from my position [[with immediate effect]].
formal.ex_us: I hereby resign from my position, [[effective immediately]].

everyday.ex: She's asked to leave [[straight away]] rather than work her three months.
everyday.ex_us: She's asked to leave [[right away]] rather than work out her three months.

informal.ex: He cleared his desk and walked out [[there and then]].
informal.ex_us: He cleared out his desk and walked out [[on the spot]].

note_fr: « With immediate effect » est britannique ; l'américain préfère « effective immediately » ou « effective [date] ». Quitter sans préavis expose en principe le salarié à devoir une indemnité, sauf dispense accordée par l'employeur.

fr: présomption de démission (en cas d'abandon de poste)
def: A French rule under which an employee who stops coming to work and does not return after formal notice from the employer is treated as having resigned.

formal.uk: to be presumed to have resigned
formal.us: to be presumed to have resigned
formal.ex: An employee who fails to return to work within the time limit set in the formal notice shall [[be presumed to have resigned]].

everyday.uk: to be treated as having resigned
everyday.us: to be treated as having resigned
everyday.ex: If he doesn't come back by the deadline, he'll [[be treated as having resigned]], which means no unemployment benefit.
everyday.ex_us: If he doesn't come back by the deadline, he'll [[be treated as having resigned]], which means no unemployment benefits.

collocations: to send a formal notice to return to work
note_fr: Aux États-Unis, beaucoup de règlements intérieurs prévoient qu'une absence injustifiée de quelques jours vaut « job abandonment », traité comme une démission. Au Royaume-Uni, rien de tel : l'employeur doit en principe licencier. « To rebut a presumption » = renverser une présomption. « Mise en demeure » = « formal notice ».

explain.written: Under the French présomption de démission, an employee who abandons his or her post and fails to return within the time limit set in a formal notice from the employer is presumed to have resigned, unless he or she shows a legitimate reason for the absence.
explain.spoken: In France, if someone simply stops turning up and ignores a formal letter asking them to come back, the law treats them as having resigned.

fr: rupture imputable à l'employeur à la suite d'une démission contrainte (« constructive dismissal »)
def: A situation in which an employee resigns because the employer's conduct has made it impossible to stay, and the law treats the resignation as a dismissal.

formal.ex: The Claimant resigned and brought a claim for [[constructive dismissal]], alleging a fundamental breach of contract.
formal.ex_us: Plaintiff resigned and brought a claim for [[constructive discharge]], alleging that working conditions had become intolerable.

everyday.uk: to resign and claim constructive dismissal
everyday.us: to quit and claim constructive discharge
everyday.ex: If we cut her pay without her agreement, she could [[resign and claim constructive dismissal]].
everyday.ex_us: If we cut her pay without her agreement, she could [[quit and claim constructive discharge]].

collocations: to resign in response to the breach
note_fr: « Constructive » ne veut pas dire « constructif » : en droit, c'est « réputé tel par interprétation ». Au Royaume-Uni, il faut une violation fondamentale du contrat par l'employeur ; aux États-Unis, des conditions de travail objectivement intolérables. Les notions françaises les plus proches sont la prise d'acte et la résiliation judiciaire.

term.uk: termination by the employee for the employer's breach
term.us: termination by the employee for the employer's breach

ipa.uk: /ˌtɜːmɪˈneɪʃ(ə)n baɪ ði ɪmˈplɔɪiː fə ði ɪmˈplɔɪəz briːtʃ/
ipa.us: /ˌtɜːrmɪˈneɪʃ(ə)n baɪ ði ɪmˈplɔɪiː fər ði ɪmˈplɔɪərz briːtʃ/

def: A French mechanism by which an employee ends the contract immediately, blaming serious breaches by the employer, and then asks the court to rule on the consequences.

formal.uk: to terminate the contract on the grounds of the employer's breach
formal.us: to terminate the contract on the grounds of the employer's breach
formal.ex: By letter of 12 January, the Employee [[terminated the contract on the grounds of the employer's breach]] of its obligations.
formal.ex_us: By letter of January 12, the Employee [[terminated the contract on the grounds of the employer's breach]] of its obligations.

everyday.uk: to walk out and blame the employer
everyday.us: to walk out and blame the employer
everyday.ex: In effect, she [[walked out and blamed the employer]]; now a court decides whether she was right to.

collocations: to take note of the termination
to have the effects of a resignation
note_fr: Ne traduisez pas mot à mot (« taking of act »). Pour un Britannique, dites : « it works rather like constructive dismissal ». Différence clé : si les manquements ne sont pas jugés assez graves, la prise d'acte produit les effets d'une démission, et le salarié peut devoir le préavis.

explain.written: The prise d'acte is a form of termination by which the employee ends the contract with immediate effect on account of the employer's serious breaches; the labour court then decides whether it takes effect as an unfair dismissal or as a resignation.
explain.spoken: It's the French cousin of constructive dismissal: the employee leaves at once, saying the employer is at fault, and a court later decides whether that counts as a dismissal or a resignation.

fr: résiliation judiciaire du contrat de travail
def: A French procedure in which an employee who is still in post asks the labour court to end the contract because of the employer's serious breaches.

formal.uk: to apply to the court for termination of the contract
formal.us: to petition the court for termination of the contract
formal.ex: The Employee has [[applied to the court for termination of the contract]] on the ground of unpaid overtime.
formal.ex_us: The Employee has [[petitioned the court for termination of the contract]] on the ground of unpaid overtime.

everyday.uk: to ask the court to end the contract
everyday.us: to ask the court to end the contract
everyday.ex: He's still working for us, but he's [[asked the court to end the contract]] and award him damages.

collocations: to remain in post pending the decision
note_fr: « Resiliation » n'existe pas ; « rescission » désigne l'anéantissement rétroactif d'un contrat, ce qui est autre chose. Aucun équivalent en common law, où le salarié doit d'abord démissionner pour agir. Le salarié continue de travailler pendant la procédure, ce qui surprend toujours un client anglo-saxon.

explain.written: Résiliation judiciaire is an action by which an employee, while remaining in post, asks the labour court to terminate the employment contract on account of the employer's serious breaches; if granted, it takes effect as an unfair dismissal.
explain.spoken: Here the employee doesn't resign. They stay in the job and ask the court to end the contract because the employer hasn't kept its side of the bargain.

fr: manquement suffisamment grave (pour empêcher la poursuite du contrat)
def: A breach of contract so serious that the other party is entitled to treat the contract as ended.

formal.ex: A unilateral reduction in pay will ordinarily amount to a [[repudiatory breach]] of the contract of employment.
formal.ex_us: A unilateral reduction in pay may constitute a [[material breach]] of the employment agreement.

everyday.uk: to go to the root of the contract
everyday.us: to go to the heart of the contract
everyday.ex: Changing someone's hours slightly is one thing; halving their pay [[goes to the root of the contract]].
everyday.ex_us: Changing someone's hours slightly is one thing; cutting their pay in half [[goes to the heart of the contract]].

collocations: the implied term of mutual trust and confidence
note_fr: « Repudiatory » est du pur droit anglais ; l'Américain parle de « material breach ». En droit français, le critère est un manquement suffisamment grave pour empêcher la poursuite du contrat. « The last straw » (la goutte d'eau) est aussi une notion juridique britannique : le dernier d'une série d'incidents.

fr: produire les effets d'un licenciement sans cause réelle et sérieuse

term.uk: to take effect as an unfair dismissal
term.us: to take effect as a wrongful termination

ipa.uk: /tə teɪk ɪˈfekt əz ən ʌnˈfeə dɪsˈmɪs(ə)l/
ipa.us: /tə teɪk ɪˈfekt əz ə ˈrɔːŋf(ə)l ˌtɜːrmɪˈneɪʃ(ə)n/

def: To have the same legal consequences as a dismissal without a valid reason, in particular an award of compensation.

formal.uk: to take effect as an unfair dismissal
formal.us: to take effect as a dismissal without valid cause
formal.ex: Where the breaches are established, the termination shall [[take effect as an unfair dismissal]].
formal.ex_us: Where the breaches are established, the termination shall [[take effect as a dismissal without valid cause]].

everyday.uk: to count as an unfair dismissal
everyday.us: to count as an unfair dismissal
everyday.ex: If the court sides with her, it [[counts as an unfair dismissal]] and we pay compensation.

collocations: to be treated as a dismissal
to have the effects of a resignation
note_fr: « Unfair dismissal » est une notion légale britannique, employée par commodité pour le licenciement sans cause réelle et sérieuse. Aux États-Unis, l'expression n'a pas de sens général du fait de l'emploi « at-will » ; « wrongful termination » y vise une rupture illégale (discrimination, représailles). Explicitez toujours.

def: To be made to leave a job by pressure rather than by an open decision to dismiss.

formal.ex: The Claimant maintains that she was [[compelled to resign]] by the conduct of her line manager.
formal.ex_us: Plaintiff maintains that she was [[compelled to resign]] by the conduct of her supervisor.

everyday.ex: He didn't jump; he was [[forced out]] after the reorganisation.
everyday.ex_us: He didn't quit; he was [[forced out]] after the reorganization.

informal.ex: Everyone could see she was being [[managed out]].

note_fr: « Pushed to the exit » est un calque. « To be managed out » est du jargon RH : écarter quelqu'un par la gestion (objectifs, mise à l'écart) sans licenciement franc. « Did he jump or was he pushed? » est la question rituelle.

def: To stop working for an employer, for whatever reason.

formal.uk: to cease to be employed by the Company
formal.us: to cease to be employed by the Company
formal.ex: Upon [[ceasing to be employed by the Company]], the Employee shall return all Company property.

everyday.ex: She's [[leaving the company]] at the end of June after twelve years.
everyday.ex_us: She's [[leaving the company]] at the end of June after twelve years here.

informal.ex: I've had six good years here, but it's time to [[move on]].

collocations: to leave of one's own accord
note_fr: « To quit the company » se comprend surtout aux États-Unis et signifie démissionner, pas simplement partir. « To leave » est transitif : « she left the company », jamais « she left from the company ». « Of one's own accord » = de son propre chef.

def: A person who is leaving or has just left an organisation.

formal.ex: A [[departing employee]] must return all equipment on or before the last day of employment.

everyday.ex: Payroll needs the list of this month's [[leavers]] by the 20th.
everyday.ex_us: Payroll needs the list of this month's [[departing employees]] by the 20th.

note_fr: « Leaver » est britannique ; l'Américain dit « departing employee » ou, en jargon RH, « separating employee ». « Joiners and leavers » = entrées et sorties. « Outgoing » se dit du titulaire sortant d'un poste (« the outgoing CFO »), « incoming » de son successeur.

fr: rupture du contrat de travail (terme neutre, quel qu'en soit le motif)
def: The ending of the working relationship, whether by dismissal, resignation, retirement or agreement.

formal.ex: Upon [[termination of employment]], howsoever arising, the following provisions shall apply.
formal.ex_us: Upon [[separation from employment]] for any reason, the following provisions shall apply.

everyday.ex: The policy sets out what happens [[when someone leaves]], whatever the reason.

note_fr: Aux États-Unis, « termination » employé seul évoque le licenciement (« he was terminated »), d'où le mot neutre « separation », avec la distinction « voluntary / involuntary separation ». Au Royaume-Uni, « termination » reste neutre. Évitez « rupture », qui évoque en anglais une hernie ou une canalisation.

def: The final day on which a departing employee actually comes to work.

formal.ex: Your [[last day of employment]] will be Friday 28 March.
formal.ex_us: Your [[last day of employment]] will be Friday, March 28.

everyday.ex: My [[last day]] is the 28th, but I'm using up holiday from the 14th.
everyday.ex_us: My [[last day]] is the 28th, but I'm using up vacation from the 14th.

collocations: to use up one's remaining holiday
one's last day in the office
to leave at the end of the month
note_fr: Le dernier jour travaillé et la date de fin du contrat ne coïncident pas toujours (congés soldés, dispense de préavis) : précisez « last day in the office » ou « last day of employment ». Format des dates : « 28 March » (UK), « March 28 » (US).

fr: se faire débaucher / être approché(e) par un chasseur de têtes
def: To be approached and persuaded to leave one's job for another employer.

formal.uk: to be approached by a competitor
formal.us: to be approached by a competitor
formal.ex: The Employee informed the Company that she had [[been approached by a competitor]].

everyday.ex: She wasn't looking; she was [[headhunted]] by one of the big consultancies.
everyday.ex_us: She wasn't looking; she was [[recruited away]] by one of the big consulting firms.

informal.ex: That's the third engineer we've had [[poached]] this year.

note_fr: « To debauch » signifie « débaucher » au sens moral : à proscrire absolument. « To poach » (braconner) est le mot familier, des deux côtés de l'Atlantique. « To jump ship » = quitter le navire pour la concurrence.

def: To leave an important position, usually voluntarily or by agreement.

formal.ex: Mr Laurent will [[relinquish his position]] as Managing Director on 31 December.
formal.ex_us: Mr. Laurent will [[relinquish his position]] as Chief Executive Officer on December 31.

everyday.ex: The finance director is [[stepping down]] at the end of the year.
everyday.ex_us: The CFO is [[stepping down]] at the end of the year.

informal.ex: After twenty years at the top, he's decided to [[bow out]].

collocations: to step down from the board
note_fr: « To step down » se dit d'un dirigeant ou d'un élu, pas d'un salarié ordinaire. « To stand down » en est la variante britannique. « To step aside » suggère qu'on laisse la place, parfois provisoirement. Ne confondez pas avec « to step back » (prendre du recul).

def: To stop working permanently, usually because one has reached a certain age.

formal.ex: The Employee has informed the Company of her intention to [[take retirement]] on 30 September.
formal.ex_us: The Employee has informed the Company of her intention to [[retire]] on September 30.

everyday.ex: He's [[retiring]] next spring after thirty years with the firm.
everyday.ex_us: He's [[retiring]] next spring after thirty years with the company.

informal.ex: I'll be sixty-four in May, and I think it's time to [[call it a day]].

note_fr: « To retire » et non « to go to retirement » ; « to retreat » signifie battre en retraite. Le retraité est « a retired person », « a pensioner » (UK) ou « a retiree » (US). Le départ à la retraite à l'initiative du salarié se dit simplement « voluntary retirement ».

def: Retirement that the employer imposes on an employee because of age.

formal.ex: Under French law, [[compulsory retirement]] may be imposed without the employee's consent only from the age of seventy.
formal.ex_us: Under French law, [[mandatory retirement]] may be imposed without the employee's consent only from the age of seventy.

everyday.ex: You can't just [[make someone retire]] at sixty-five; in most cases that would be age discrimination.

informal.uk: to put someone out to grass
informal.us: to put someone out to pasture
informal.ex: He's sixty-six and has no intention of being [[put out to grass]].
informal.ex_us: He's sixty-six and has no intention of being [[put out to pasture]].

note_fr: Grande différence entre systèmes. France : mise à la retraite d'office possible à partir de 70 ans, et avant cet âge seulement avec l'accord du salarié. Royaume-Uni : plus d'âge de retraite par défaut ; imposer un départ suppose une justification objective. États-Unis : la loi fédérale interdit en principe la retraite obligatoire, sauf exceptions étroites.

fr: âge légal de départ à la retraite
def: The age from which a person may claim the public retirement pension.

formal.ex: The Employee will reach the French [[statutory retirement age]] in the course of next year.

everyday.ex: She's two years off [[state pension age]] and would rather not leave before then.
everyday.ex_us: She's two years away from [[full retirement age]] and would rather not leave before then.

note_fr: Les notions ne se recouvrent pas : en France, l'âge légal ouvre le droit de partir, pas forcément à taux plein ; au Royaume-Uni, la « State Pension age » est l'âge de perception de la pension publique, sans lien avec le contrat de travail ; aux États-Unis, la « full retirement age » est celle de la pension fédérale complète.

def: A retirement pension paid at the maximum rate, without any reduction for missing contribution periods.

formal.ex: The Employee will qualify for a [[full-rate pension]] once she has completed the required number of contribution quarters.
formal.ex_us: The Employee will qualify for [[full retirement benefits]] once she has completed the required contribution period.

everyday.ex: If he hangs on another eighteen months, he'll get his [[full pension]].

collocations: to qualify for a full pension
note_fr: « Full rate retirement » est un calque. En France, le taux plein dépend de la durée d'assurance (trimestres) ou de l'âge ; expliquez-le, car la logique des « quarters » est inconnue ailleurs. Aux États-Unis, « benefits » désigne ici la pension fédérale (Social Security).

fr: indemnité de départ à la retraite
def: In France, a lump sum that the employer pays to an employee who retires, the amount of which depends on length of service.

formal.ex: On retirement, the Employee shall receive the [[retirement payment]] provided for by law or, if more favourable, by the applicable collective agreement.
formal.ex_us: On retirement, the Employee shall receive the [[retirement payment]] provided for by law or, if more favorable, by the applicable collective agreement.

everyday.ex: After twenty-five years' service, she's entitled to a [[lump sum on retirement]] from the company.
everyday.ex_us: After twenty-five years of service, she's entitled to a [[lump sum at retirement]] from the company.

note_fr: Ne dites pas « retirement indemnity ». Rien d'équivalent n'est imposé par la loi au Royaume-Uni ou aux États-Unis, où l'employeur finance plutôt un régime de retraite pendant la carrière. À ne pas confondre avec la pension elle-même (« pension »), versée par les caisses.

explain.written: The indemnité de départ à la retraite is a one-off payment made by the employer to an employee who retires; its amount is set by law or by the collective agreement and increases with length of service.
explain.spoken: In France the employer pays a one-off lump sum when someone retires. It's separate from the pension, and it grows with length of service.

def: Retirement before the usual age.

formal.ex: Employees with long careers may be eligible for [[early retirement]] under the conditions laid down by law.

everyday.ex: He'd love to [[retire early]], but he can't afford to yet.

note_fr: « Anticipated retirement » signifie « la retraite que l'on prévoit », pas « anticipée ». « To take early retirement » est la collocation usuelle. Au Royaume-Uni, « ill-health retirement » désigne le départ anticipé pour raison de santé prévu par certains régimes.

def: An arrangement under which an employee nearing retirement reduces working hours gradually, sometimes while drawing part of the pension.

formal.ex: Under the [[phased retirement]] arrangement, the Employee will work part-time and receive a proportion of her pension.

everyday.ex: She'd like to [[wind down]] gradually: four days a week next year, then three.

informal.ex: Going part-time is a nice way to [[ease into retirement]].

note_fr: « Progressive retirement » se comprend mais n'est pas idiomatique : dites « phased » ou, au Royaume-Uni, « flexible retirement ». « To wind down » (prononcé « waɪnd ») = ralentir progressivement son activité ; à ne pas confondre avec « to wind up » (liquider, clôturer).

fr: liquider / faire valoir ses droits à la retraite
def: To start receiving one's retirement pension.

formal.ex: The Employee has informed the Company that he intends to [[claim his pension]] with effect from 1 October.
formal.ex_us: The Employee has informed the Company that he intends to [[claim his retirement benefits]] effective October 1.

everyday.ex: She could [[draw her pension]] now, but it would be reduced.
everyday.ex_us: She could [[collect her pension]] now, but it would be reduced.

note_fr: « To liquidate one's pension » voudrait dire la convertir en liquidités, voire la dilapider : faux ami. « To draw » est britannique, « to collect » américain. « Pension » en anglais désigne la retraite versée, jamais une pension de famille ni une pension alimentaire (« maintenance », « alimony »).

def: The French rules allowing a retired person to take up paid work again while continuing to receive a pension.

formal.uk: combining employment with a retirement pension
formal.us: combining employment with a retirement pension
formal.ex: The rules on [[combining employment with a retirement pension]] allow a retiree to be re-engaged by a former employer, subject to certain conditions.

everyday.uk: to carry on working after retiring
everyday.ex: Plenty of consultants [[carry on working after retiring]] and draw their pension at the same time.
everyday.ex_us: Plenty of consultants [[keep working after retiring]] and collect their pension at the same time.

collocations: to return to work after retirement
note_fr: « Cumulation » n'a pas ce sens. La notion intrigue les Anglo-Saxons, chez qui travailler en percevant une pension privée ne pose en général aucune question particulière : expliquez qu'en France le contrat est rompu au départ à la retraite et qu'il faut en conclure un nouveau.

explain.written: Cumul emploi-retraite is the set of French rules under which a person who has claimed a retirement pension may resume paid employment and receive both the pension and a salary.
explain.spoken: In France you can retire, start drawing your pension and then go back to work, but there are rules about how you do it.

fr: solde de tout compte (sommes versées à la fin du contrat)
def: Everything the employer still owes an employee when the job ends: salary, untaken holiday, bonus and any termination payment.

formal.uk: final payment of salary and accrued entitlements
formal.ex: The [[final payment of salary and accrued entitlements]] will be made on the Termination Date.
formal.ex_us: [[Final wages]], including accrued and unused vacation where required by law, will be paid on the Separation Date.

everyday.ex: Your [[final pay]] will include eight days of untaken holiday.
everyday.ex_us: Your [[final paycheck]] will include eight days of unused vacation.

collocations: to be paid up to and including
note_fr: Aux États-Unis, le délai de remise du « final paycheck » dépend de chaque État, et il est parfois très court. « Payslip » (UK) / « pay stub » (US) = bulletin de paie. « Balance of all accounts » est un calque incompréhensible.

fr: reçu pour solde de tout compte
def: A French document, drawn up by the employer and signed by the departing employee, listing the sums paid at the end of the contract.

formal.ex: The Employee may challenge the [[receipt for final payment]] within six months of signing it; thereafter it discharges the employer in respect of the sums listed.

everyday.uk: to sign for one's final pay
everyday.us: to sign for one's final pay
everyday.ex: You'll be asked to [[sign for your final pay]], but that doesn't stop you querying the figures later.

note_fr: Prononciation : le « p » de « receipt » est muet. Ce reçu n'est pas une transaction : il ne libère l'employeur que pour les sommes qui y figurent. Aucun équivalent britannique ou américain ; n'employez pas « full and final settlement », qui désigne un véritable accord de règlement.

explain.written: The reçu pour solde de tout compte is a statement of the sums paid to the employee on termination, which the employee signs by way of receipt and may challenge within six months.
explain.spoken: It's simply a signed receipt listing what the employee was paid on leaving. It isn't a waiver of claims.

def: A document the French employer must give every departing employee, stating the dates of employment and the positions held.

formal.ex: The Company shall issue the Employee with a [[certificate of employment]] on the last day of the contract.
formal.ex_us: The Company shall issue the Employee a [[certificate of employment]] on the last day of the contract.

everyday.ex: It's just [[proof of employment]]: dates and job titles, with no comment on performance.

note_fr: « Work certificate » évoque plutôt un diplôme professionnel. Rien de tel au Royaume-Uni (où le salarié reçoit un formulaire fiscal, le P45) ni aux États-Unis, où l'on demande au besoin une « employment verification letter ». Ce n'est pas une « reference » : aucune appréciation n'y figure.

explain.written: The certificat de travail is a mandatory document issued by the employer at the end of any employment contract, stating the dates of employment and the nature of the positions held.
explain.spoken: Every employee who leaves a French company gets a certificate confirming when they worked there and in what role. It's purely factual.

fr: attestation destinée à France Travail (attestation employeur)

term.uk: employer's certificate for the unemployment agency
term.us: employer's certificate for the unemployment agency

def: A document the French employer must give the departing employee and send to the public employment service, so that entitlement to unemployment benefit can be assessed.

formal.uk: employer's certificate for the unemployment agency
formal.us: employer's certificate for the unemployment agency
formal.ex: The [[employer's certificate for the unemployment agency]] states the reason for termination and the remuneration paid over the reference period.

everyday.us: the form for the unemployment office
everyday.ex: Without [[the form for the jobcentre]], she can't get her claim started.
everyday.ex_us: Without [[the form for the unemployment office]], she can't get her claim started.

collocations: to state the reason for termination
to issue the certificate without delay
note_fr: France Travail (ex-Pôle emploi) se présente comme « the French public employment service ». « Attestation » existe en anglais mais désigne un acte de certification solennel : préférez « certificate » ou « form ». « Jobcentre » est britannique.

explain.written: The attestation France Travail is a certificate which the employer must provide at the end of every contract, to the employee and to the public employment service, recording the reason for termination and the pay on which unemployment benefit is calculated.
explain.spoken: It's the form the employer fills in for the unemployment agency. The employee needs it to claim benefit.

def: The documents an employer gives an employee when the job ends.

formal.ex: The [[termination documents]] will be handed to the Employee on the Termination Date.
formal.ex_us: The [[separation documents]] will be provided to the Employee on the Separation Date.

everyday.ex: HR will send you all your [[leaving paperwork]] with your final payslip.
everyday.ex_us: HR will send you all your [[separation paperwork]] with your final pay stub.

note_fr: « Paperwork » est indénombrable : « the paperwork is ready », jamais « the paperworks ». En France, trois documents sont obligatoires : certificat de travail, attestation France Travail et reçu pour solde de tout compte. Au Royaume-Uni, l'essentiel se résume au P45.

term.uk: payment in lieu of untaken holiday

def: Money paid at the end of the contract for paid leave the employee has earned but not taken.

formal.uk: payment in lieu of accrued but untaken holiday
formal.us: payment for accrued but unused vacation
formal.ex: The Employee shall receive a [[payment in lieu of accrued but untaken holiday]] as at the Termination Date.
formal.ex_us: The Employee shall receive [[payment for accrued but unused vacation]] as of the Separation Date.

everyday.uk: to be paid for untaken holiday
everyday.us: to be paid out for unused vacation
everyday.ex: You've got six days left, so you'll [[be paid for untaken holiday]] in your final salary.
everyday.ex_us: You have six days left, so you'll [[be paid out for unused vacation]] in your final paycheck.

note_fr: « In lieu of » (à la place de) se prononce « in lyou » ou « in loo ». « To accrue » = acquérir progressivement (des droits). Aux États-Unis, le paiement des congés non pris dépend de la loi de chaque État et de la politique de l'entreprise.

def: The process of passing one's work, files and responsibilities to the person taking over.

formal.ex: The Employee shall cooperate in ensuring an [[orderly handover]] of his duties and files.
formal.ex_us: The Employee shall cooperate in ensuring an [[orderly transition]] of his duties and files.

everyday.ex: Let's block out his last two weeks for the [[handover]].
everyday.ex_us: Let's block out his last two weeks for the [[handoff]].

collocations: to do a handover with one's successor
note_fr: « Handover » (nom, en un mot) est surtout britannique ; l'Américain parle de « transition » ou de « handoff ». Le verbe s'écrit en deux mots : « to hand over ». « Passation » n'existe pas en anglais.

def: To give one's files and responsibilities to a colleague or successor before leaving.
