formal.ex: During the notice period, the Employee shall [[transfer his responsibilities]] to the person designated by the Company.

everyday.ex: I'm [[handing over to]] Priya, so please copy her in from now on.
everyday.ex_us: I'm [[handing off to]] Priya, so please copy her from now on.

informal.ex: Right, time to [[pass the baton]]. She's all yours, Priya.

collocations: to bring someone up to speed
note_fr: Symétrie utile : « to hand over TO someone » (transmettre à) / « to take over FROM someone » (reprendre de). « To bring someone up to speed » = mettre quelqu'un au courant. « To copy someone in » (UK) / « to copy someone » ou « to cc » (US).

def: A conversation with a departing employee to understand why he or she is leaving and what the organisation could improve.

formal.ex: All departing employees are invited to attend an [[exit interview]] with a member of the HR team.

everyday.ex: Nothing surprising came out of her [[exit interview]]: pay, and no prospect of promotion.

informal.ex: It's not a formal thing, just a quick [[exit chat]] over coffee.

note_fr: Seul cas, hors recrutement, où « interview » convient en RH. On « conducts » ou « holds » un entretien, on ne le « makes » pas. « Candid » signifie « franc », non « candide ». Pratique facultative dans les trois pays.

def: Giving back everything that belongs to the employer, such as a laptop, phone, access badge, car and documents.

formal.uk: to return all property belonging to the Company
formal.us: to return all property belonging to the Company
formal.ex: On or before the Termination Date, the Employee shall [[return all property belonging to the Company]], including any copies of documents.
formal.ex_us: On or before the Separation Date, the Employee shall [[return all property belonging to the Company]], including any copies of documents.

everyday.ex: Don't forget to [[hand back]] your laptop and security pass on your last day.
everyday.ex_us: Don't forget to [[turn in]] your laptop and badge on your last day.

collocations: to delete company data from personal devices
note_fr: « Material » est un faux ami : c'est la matière ou la documentation, pas le matériel ; dites « equipment » (indénombrable) ou « property ». « Restitution » existe mais relève du droit des obligations. Badge : « pass » (UK), « badge » (US).

def: To stop a departing employee from being able to use the company's IT systems and premises.

formal.ex: The Company reserves the right to [[revoke access rights]] to its systems at close of business on the Termination Date.
formal.ex_us: The Company reserves the right to [[revoke access rights]] to its systems at close of business on the Separation Date.

everyday.ex: IT will [[cut off his access]] at six o'clock on Friday, so make sure the handover's done by then.

informal.ex: They [[locked her out]] of her email before she'd even left the building.

collocations: to set up an out-of-office message
note_fr: « Access » est indénombrable dans ce sens : « to revoke access », pas « the accesses ». « To deactivate / disable an account » ; « to desactivate » n'existe pas. Couper les accès sans prévenir pendant une négociation peut être interprété comme une pression.

def: Money paid by the state or an insurance scheme to people who have lost their job and are looking for work.

formal.ex: A mutual termination agreement gives access to [[unemployment benefit]] on the same terms as a dismissal.
formal.ex_us: A mutual termination agreement gives access to [[unemployment insurance benefits]] on the same terms as a dismissal.

everyday.ex: Will she get [[unemployment benefit]] if she leaves by agreement?
everyday.ex_us: Will she get [[unemployment]] if she leaves by agreement?

informal.ex: He was on [[the dole]] for six months before he found something.
informal.ex_us: He was on [[unemployment]] for six months before he found something.

note_fr: « Unemployment allocations » est un calque. Singulier indénombrable au Royaume-Uni (« unemployment benefit »), pluriel aux États-Unis. Les systèmes diffèrent beaucoup : assurance généreuse et proportionnelle au salaire en France, allocation forfaitaire modeste au Royaume-Uni, régime propre à chaque État aux États-Unis.

term.uk: to be eligible for unemployment benefit
term.us: to be eligible for unemployment benefits

def: To meet the conditions for receiving payments while out of work.

formal.uk: to give rise to entitlement to unemployment benefit
formal.us: to give rise to entitlement to unemployment benefits
formal.ex: Resignation does not ordinarily [[give rise to entitlement to unemployment benefit]] under the French scheme.
formal.ex_us: Resignation does not ordinarily [[give rise to entitlement to unemployment benefits]] under the French system.

everyday.ex: If you resign, you won't normally [[qualify for unemployment benefit]]; with a mutual termination, you will.
everyday.ex_us: If you quit, you won't normally [[qualify for unemployment]]; with a mutual termination, you will.

collocations: to leave voluntarily without good reason
note_fr: « To open rights » est un calque. C'est souvent l'argument décisif pour le salarié français : la rupture conventionnelle ouvre droit au chômage, la démission en principe non. Aux États-Unis aussi, celui qui démissionne sans motif légitime est en général exclu ; au Royaume-Uni, il risque une suspension de ses allocations.

def: To sign up officially with the public employment service in order to look for work and claim benefit.

formal.us: to file a claim for unemployment benefits
formal.ex: Benefit is payable only once the former employee has [[registered as a jobseeker]] with the public employment service.
formal.ex_us: Benefits are payable only once the former employee has [[filed a claim for unemployment benefits]] with the state agency.

everyday.ex: [[Register with the jobcentre]] as soon as your contract ends; don't wait for the paperwork.
everyday.ex_us: [[File for unemployment]] as soon as your employment ends; don't wait for the paperwork.

informal.ex: I never thought I'd have to [[sign on]] at fifty-two.
informal.ex_us: I never thought I'd have to [[go on unemployment]] at fifty-two.

note_fr: « Job demander » et « to inscribe oneself » n'existent pas. « To sign on » est britannique et familier (à ne pas confondre avec « to sign up », s'inscrire à un service). « To be between jobs » est l'euphémisme élégant pour « être au chômage ».

def: A period after the end of the contract during which unemployment benefit is not yet paid.

formal.ex: Any payment in excess of the statutory minimum will extend the [[deferral period]] before benefit becomes payable.
formal.ex_us: Any payment in excess of the statutory minimum will extend the [[deferral period]] before benefits become payable.

everyday.ex: The bigger the payment, the longer the [[waiting period]] before her benefit kicks in.
everyday.ex_us: The bigger the payment, the longer the [[waiting period]] before her benefits kick in.

collocations: to factor in the waiting period
note_fr: « Carence » ne se traduit ni par « deficiency » ni par « lack ». Point à signaler dans toute négociation française : la part de l'indemnité qui dépasse le minimum légal retarde le versement des allocations, dans une limite fixée par la réglementation. « To kick in » = commencer à s'appliquer.

def: Professional help, paid for by the former employer, to assist a departing employee in finding a new job.

formal.ex: The Company shall fund [[outplacement support]] from a provider of the Employee's choice, up to a maximum of EUR 6,000 excluding VAT.
formal.ex_us: The Company shall pay for [[outplacement services]] from a provider of the Employee's choice, up to a maximum of USD 6,000.

everyday.uk: help with finding a new job
everyday.ex: The package includes six months' [[help with finding a new job]].
everyday.ex_us: The package includes six months of [[help finding a new job]].

note_fr: Le mot est anglais, mais il s'emploie surtout avec « support », « services » ou « programme / program ». « Reclassement » n'est pas « reclassification » (qui signifie changement de catégorie). CV : « CV » (UK), « résumé » (US).

fr: portabilité de la mutuelle et de la prévoyance

term.uk: continuation of health and welfare cover

def: The right of a former employee who is receiving unemployment benefit to remain covered, for a limited time, by the employer's health and welfare insurance.

formal.uk: continuation of health and welfare cover
formal.ex: The Employee shall benefit from [[continuation of health and welfare cover]], free of charge, for the period provided for by law.
formal.ex_us: The Employee shall benefit from [[continuation of health coverage]], at no cost, for the period provided for by law.

everyday.uk: to stay on the company health plan
everyday.us: to stay on the company health plan
everyday.ex: As long as you're claiming benefit, you [[stay on the company health plan]] for up to a year at no cost.
everyday.ex_us: As long as you're collecting unemployment, you [[stay on the company health plan]] for up to a year at no cost.

collocations: at no cost to the employee
note_fr: « Portability » se comprend, mais il faut expliquer le mécanisme. Comparaison utile pour un Américain : c'est l'esprit du dispositif COBRA, sauf qu'en France le maintien est gratuit pour l'ancien salarié, alors qu'aux États-Unis il paie en général la totalité de la prime. « Cover » (UK) / « coverage » (US).

explain.written: Portabilité is the statutory right of a former employee who qualifies for unemployment benefit to retain, free of charge and for a limited period, the health and welfare insurance cover provided by the former employer.
explain.spoken: If you leave and you're entitled to unemployment benefit, you keep the company's health cover for a while, at no cost.

def: An informal gathering at which colleagues say goodbye to someone who is leaving.

formal.ex: A [[farewell reception]] will be held in the boardroom on Thursday at 5 p.m.

everyday.ex: Are you coming to Marc's [[leaving drinks]] on Thursday?
everyday.ex_us: Are you coming to Marc's [[farewell party]] on Thursday?

informal.ex: We're having a little [[leaving do]] for her at the pub.
informal.ex_us: We're giving her a little [[send-off]] at the bar down the street.

collocations: to give someone a good send-off
note_fr: « A do » (UK, familier) = une fête. « A whip-round » (UK) = une collecte entre collègues ; aux États-Unis, « to take up a collection » ou « to chip in ». « Departure pot » n'a aucun sens.

fr: « good leaver » / « bad leaver » (sort des actions et stock-options selon les circonstances du départ)
def: Categories used in share and incentive plans to decide what a departing employee keeps, depending on why he or she is leaving.

formal.uk: to be treated as a good leaver
formal.us: to be treated as a good leaver
formal.ex: For the purposes of the share plan, the Employee shall [[be treated as a good leaver]] and shall retain his vested options.
formal.ex_us: For purposes of the equity plan, the Employee shall [[be treated as a good leaver]] and shall retain his vested options.

everyday.ex: Her adviser's main demand is [[good leaver]] status, so that she keeps her shares.
everyday.ex_us: Her attorney's main demand is [[good leaver]] status, so that she keeps her equity.

note_fr: Point de négociation fréquent pour les cadres dirigeants : le « bad leaver » (démission, faute) perd tout ou partie de ses titres ; le « good leaver » (retraite, invalidité, départ négocié selon le plan) les conserve. « Vested » = définitivement acquis ; « to forfeit » = perdre (un droit). Vocabulaire d'origine britannique, compris aux États-Unis.
